questions.prompt: A log-analysis function must return the index of the FIRST failed request and must preserve duplicate records. Which requirements mean you should keep sequence semantics?
questions.explanation: The first matching index depends on order/position, and preserving duplicate records means multiplicity matters. A membership-only set would lose both kinds of information.
hints: Ask what information a set would discard.

error_codes.description: A sequence requirement was missed.
A requirement that does not itself require sequence semantics was selected.

hints: The contract permits a change to each tag's case, not a change to list order or multiplicity.

questions.prompt: A dashboard loads one static daily-count array and will answer many range queries. Order the one-time prefix-state build.
questions.explanation: The leading zero represents the boundary before the first item. Each later prefix appends the previous cumulative total plus the next value.
hints: The first stored prefix is the sum of zero items.

error_codes.description: The prefix-construction steps are out of order.

questions.explanation: The prefix totals are [0, 3, 4, 8]: each boundary stores the sum of all values before it.
hints: Add one value at a time to the previous cumulative total.

error_codes.description: At least one cumulative total is incorrect.

questions.prompt: A dashboard precomputed `prefix[i] = sum(values[0:i])`. Which expression answers the half-open report range `[l,r)` without rescanning?
questions.explanation: `prefix[r]` contains everything before r; subtracting `prefix[l]` removes everything before l, leaving exactly values[l:r].
hints: Subtract the cumulative total before the range from the cumulative total after the range.

error_codes.description: The selected expression does not match the stated half-open prefix convention.

choice_feedback.correct: Correct: the two prefix boundaries isolate [l,r).
choice_feedback.off1: This mixes inclusive and half-open indexing.
choice_feedback.sum: Adding prefix values double-counts the earlier part.

choices.label: `prefix[r] - prefix[l]`
`prefix[r] - prefix[l - 1]`
`prefix[r] + prefix[l]`
`prefix[l] - prefix[r]`

questions.prompt: A dashboard stores 365 daily request counts. The data is loaded once, then thousands of queries ask for the total over different day ranges. Which approach best fits that workload?
questions.explanation: One O(n) prefix precomputation lets each static range-sum query use two prefix values. Re-summing every requested range repeats work across thousands of queries.

error_codes.description: The selected approach does not exploit the static-data/many-range-query workload.

choice_feedback.prefix: Correct: static data + many range sums is exactly the useful trade-off.
choice_feedback.rescan: This repeats the same additions across many queries.
choice_feedback.set: A set cannot represent cumulative sums.
choice_feedback.sort: Sorting destroys the day ordering and does not answer arbitrary date-range totals.

choices.label: Build prefix totals once, then subtract two boundaries per query
Rescan and sum the requested days for every query
Store the daily counts in a set
Sort all daily counts before answering ranges

questions.prompt: The code uses `prefix[i] = sum(values[0:i])` and wants the half-open range `[l, r)`. Flag the expression with the off-by-one error.
questions.explanation: Under this boundary convention, the range sum is `prefix[r] - prefix[l]`. Using `prefix[l - 1]` incorrectly mixes an inclusive-prefix formula with a half-open-prefix representation.
hints: Check the exact meaning of prefix[l] before changing the index.

error_codes.description: The mixed-indexing formula was not identified.

questions.prompt: While scanning values, the current cumulative sum is `p`. Why does finding an earlier prefix equal to `p - target` prove there is a contiguous interval ending here whose sum is `target`?
questions.explanation: The sum between two prefix boundaries is their difference. If earlier = p - target, then p - earlier = target. The earlier boundary and current boundary therefore enclose a matching contiguous interval.
hints: Write the interval sum as current_prefix - earlier_prefix.

error_codes.description: Part of the prefix-difference justification was missed.
An unnecessary positivity or ordering condition was selected.

questions.instruction: Select all statements that justify the relation.

evidence.label: A contiguous interval sum equals the difference of its two prefix boundaries

questions.prompt: When COUNTING all contiguous intervals whose sum is `target`, why is the prefix-frequency map often initialized with `{0: 1}` before scanning?
questions.explanation: The zero prefix represents the boundary before the first element. Without it, a matching interval that begins at index 0 would not find its required earlier prefix.
hints: Consider a matching interval that begins with the first value.

error_codes.description: The selected reason does not explain the boundary represented by the zero prefix.

choice_feedback.boundary: Correct: the initial zero is a real prefix boundary before any items.
choice_feedback.collision: It is unrelated to hash collision handling.
choice_feedback.sorted: It does not sort or reorder the input.
choice_feedback.positive: It is needed even when values include negatives or zeros.

choices.label: It represents the prefix before index 0, so intervals starting at index 0 can match
It prevents hash collisions
It guarantees prefix sums remain sorted
It forces every prefix sum to stay positive

questions.prompt: A time-ordered stream records signed byte deltas, such as `+120, -40, -80, ...`. You need to know whether ANY contiguous time period has net change exactly `0`. Values can be positive or negative. Which structure best matches the problem?
questions.explanation: A zero-sum interval exists exactly when the same prefix sum occurs at two different boundaries. Maintain seen prefix sums while scanning; repeated prefix state proves the intervening contiguous period sums to zero.

error_codes.description: The selected approach does not preserve the prefix-state relation for arbitrary signed values.

choice_feedback.prefixset: Correct: equal prefix sums at two boundaries imply a zero-sum interval between them.
choice_feedback.window: With positive and negative deltas, moving one boundary does not change the sum monotonically enough for a simple variable-window rule.
choice_feedback.freqvalues: Counting individual delta values does not capture cumulative interval sums.

choices.label: Maintain the running prefix sum and a set of prefix sums seen at earlier boundaries
Use a variable window that always shrinks whenever the sum becomes positive
Sort the deltas by value and scan adjacent entries
Count how many times each individual delta value occurs
